clue.text: Rob sent back school starter of tomato soup

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: the word rob written backwards
SCH is a standard abbreviation for school

indicators.note: a starter is the opening course, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of tomato

explanation.surface: A thief retreats from a school canteen that serves tomato soup as its first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a verb or a name, but it is simply the letters to turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is a Russian and Ukrainian beetroot soup, often served hot with sour cream.

clue.text: Honour long Bible books, following orders

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
to be dying for something is to long for it
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone longs for an honour while studying Bible books in faithful compliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch. 'Following orders' looks like wordplay sequencing but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is obedient does what they are told, carrying out instructions without resistance.

clue.text: Save Romeo one little bit of barbecued meat on the bone

parts.note: to spare is to save or keep back
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a little piece of a word is just a single letter of it, here its first

parts.note: just the first letter of bit

explanation.surface: A diner urges Romeo to keep back a morsel of the barbecued meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' suggests Shakespeare, but it is the radio code word for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork rib with most of the meat trimmed off, commonly barbecued.

clue.text: Sadly, the French taking over from this point

indicators.note: things that go sadly go wrong, so the letters fall out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that the French are going to be in charge from now on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' looks like a nation, but all its letters, with the cricket O, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth is an adverb meaning from now on, starting at this moment.

clue.text: Sound made when Newton breaks part of foot

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a toe is a part of the foot
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A cracking noise is heard as Newton breaks a bone in his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' suggests the scientist, but here it is the SI unit named after him, symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone is a musical sound of definite pitch, or any sound considered for its quality.

clue.text: Singers beginning to charm Egyptian god

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is used

parts.note: the first letter of charm
Horus is the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A choir starts to win over an Egyptian deity with song.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is a group of singers performing together, as in an opera or choral society.

clue.text: Transport sheep in rickety cart

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a rickety thing is shaky and falling apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer moves a sheep about in a wobbly old cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like a verb with sheep as its object, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a passenger vehicle running on rails along a street, a form of public transport.

clue.text: Doorman runs after black cat

indicators.note: after sets the first word's piece behind the pieces that follow it in the clue

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A doorman flees from a black cat crossing his path.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is the snow leopard, a wild cat. 'Runs' reads as a verb but supplies the cricket abbreviation, placed after the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is a security guard on the door of a club or bar who ejects troublemakers.

clue.text: Fancy tailor clothes husband, old rake!

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes inside
fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters are arranged in a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
H is the abbreviation for husband
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A smart tailor dresses a husband who is a former womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old rake' reads as one phrase, but old only supplies the final letter; 'clothes' is a verb meaning wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, from a character in a Restoration play, is a byword for a seducer of women, a libertine.

clue.text: Marvellous painter, reportedly says the Princess Royal

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the answer is what the words sound like

parts.note: 'sez' is a colloquial says, and Anne is the Princess Royal

explanation.surface: Princess Anne declares an artist to be marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Princess Royal is the title held by Anne, the late Queen's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cézanne was a French Post-Impressionist painter, widely regarded as one of the greats.

clue.text: Tipsy supporter, according to Spooner, one such as Charon

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds trade places

parts.note: tipsy is merry and a supporter is a fan; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A drunken football fan is likened to a mythological figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of merry fan gives ferry man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Charon rows the souls of the dead across the river Styx, so he is a ferryman.

clue.text: Distant rounds of applause welcoming 1,000 agricultural workers

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: far means distant
to give someone a big hand is to applaud them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Far-off applause greets a thousand people working on farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmhands are labourers employed on a farm, doing agricultural work.

clue.text: British maintenance corps commandeering island rowing boat

indicators.note: to commandeer is to seize and take in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, the British Army's maintenance corps
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: British army engineers seize an island in a military raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme is an ancient galley propelled by two banks of oars, so a rowed warship.

clue.text: Free space newly fitted with one emergency exit

indicators.note: something newly fitted has been reassembled, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An empty area has just been equipped with an emergency exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is a staircase or route allowing people to leave a building in an emergency.

clue.text: Provoke former partner, bitter at English

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
acerb is a variant of acerbic, sharp or bitter
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone goads an ex who is resentful about the English.
explanation.definitionFit: To exacerbate is to make worse or aggravate, close to provoking or inflaming a situation.

clue.text: One is against unfrocked six-footer seen praying

indicators.note: unfrocked means stripped of clothing, so the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: the praying mantis is an insect, and insects have six legs

explanation.surface: A defrocked priest is seen at prayer, an apparent opponent of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer seen praying' suggests a tall cleric, but it is an insect with six feet: the praying mantis.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person opposed to something, a noun for an opponent.

clue.text: Where to sleep soundly, notice a spot for life

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a berth is a bunk on a ship or train
to mark something is to notice it

explanation.surface: A bunk to sleep deeply in, and a notice reserving a spot for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like it goes with sleep (sleep soundly), but it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthmark is a blemish on the skin present from birth that usually stays for life.

clue.text: As a breakfast dish, cooked Gere egg sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling inside, so the answer sits within the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cooked, all of Gere and the start of egg

explanation.surface: Richard Gere cooks eggs in a sandwich for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' looks like an anagram signal for Gere egg, but there is no anagram: the answer is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of rice, flaked smoked fish and boiled eggs, traditionally eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Talk of Moroccan city soldier being shot at?

indicators.note: talk of means the word as spoken, so its sound is used rather than its spelling

parts.note: Fez is a city in Morocco
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier hears gossip about a Moroccan city while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is pronounced 'fez-ant'. 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, which is why the definition fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheasant is a game bird, a creature that shooting parties take aim at.

clue.text: Live in an outbuilding, mortified

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding
to live is to exist, as in I am

explanation.surface: Someone living in a garden shed feels humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' is used in the sense of be or exist, giving the verb form 'am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling embarrassment or guilt, much the same as mortified.

clue.text: Try Hugo pants, a cultured product

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or bad, so the letters are in a poor order needing rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper is urged to try trousers from a stylish fashion brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as trousers (Hugo is a fashion label), but in British slang pants means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is made by fermenting milk with bacterial cultures, so it is a cultured food.

clue.text: Take a bite of white chocolate as a prelude to foxtrot

indicators.note: a bite is a small piece taken from inside something, so the answer is a stretch of the words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of white and the start of chocolate

explanation.surface: Someone nibbles white chocolate before taking to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxtrot' looks like the dance, but it is the code word for F in the radio alphabet, and the answer is the code word just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet Echo stands for E, which comes immediately before Foxtrot for F.

clue.text: 14lb layer granite hollowed out in rock collection

parts.note: a stone is an imperial weight of fourteen pounds
a hen lays eggs

indicators.note: something hollowed out has its inside removed, leaving only its outer shell

parts.note: the outer letters of granite

explanation.surface: A heavy slab of granite is laid hollowed out within a stone circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' suggests a stratum of rock, but read as one who lays it is a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric ring of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, a famous assembly of rocks.

clue.text: Volunteer to pay attention when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so letters move from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A volunteer is told to listen carefully while out on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of the word for paying attention move round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service of one's own accord, to volunteer.

clue.text: Each German from the east collects good music

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each

indicators.note: to collect is to take in and hold, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: GER is the abbreviation for German
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Every German heading west picks up some good music.
explanation.definitionFit: Reggae is a style of popular music that originated in Jamaica in the late 1960s.

clue.text: Greek who went for a dip sick, beset by pains

definitions.text: Greek who went for a dip

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A Greek man takes a swim while feeling ill and full of pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went for a dip' sounds like a swim, but it alludes to the myth of his mother dipping him in the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles, the Greek hero, was dipped in the river Styx as a baby, which made him invulnerable except at the heel.

clue.text: Style the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fashion piece about Spanish style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a magazine piece, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan means flair or stylish energy, a dash in the way something is done.

clue.text: Means to follow objective target for driver

indicators.note: to follow puts the first-named piece behind the one that comes after it

parts.note: objective means fair and impartial
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Talk of a method and objective in aiming at a target while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun meaning goal, but it is the adjective meaning unbiased. The driver is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairway is the closely mown area between tee and green, where a golfer hitting with a driver aims.

clue.text: Centaurs ravaged old Italian

indicators.note: something ravaged has been wrecked, so the letters are left in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mythical half-horse creatures lay waste to an ancient Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient people of central Italy, before Roman dominance.

clue.text: Chaps in police force first to order souvenir

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
chaps are men

indicators.note: first to means just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of order

explanation.surface: Police officers are the first to call for order, and keep a memento.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the everyday name for London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event, just as a souvenir is.
